title: The slide into Edit mode draws every frame, like the slide back to View
goal: Going from View to Edit, the tool bar, tracks and panel slide in at a low frame rate: the window draws a new frame only every 10 to 60 ms while they move, even on a short recording, so the slide looks choppy. Going back to View is smooth. Make the slide into Edit as smooth as the slide out.
notes: Found 2026-09-29 by switching-a-long-recording-to-edit-mode-draws-it, after it split the Cmd-2 key pass up (EditModeArrival). Reproduce: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/segmented-thumb-film-walk.json, then read /tmp/photonz-playtest/segmented-thumb-film/1-view-to-edit.json frames. Output 2026-09-29: View to Edit thumb positions change at ms 289, 351, 360, 375, 411, 421, 429, 437, 491, 500 (steps of 10 to 62ms); Edit to View changes every ~9ms from 256 to 495. Long captioned sample (Scripts/playtest/view-to-edit-on-a-long-recording-walk.json): wait after Cmd-2 reads mainBusy 633 to 758ms over 0.8s, with passes of 30 to 50ms all through the 250ms slide; after Cmd-1 about 530ms. Suspects: the panel move transition narrows the canvas every frame (HStack), so the canvas, its viewport refit, the tool bar fit budget (reconcileToolbarCount) and the whole panel lay out per frame; the dock growing relays the grid every frame. Idea: slide the panel with an offset over a fixed canvas width and refit once at the end.
acceptance: Filming the View | Edit thumb on Cmd-2 (segmented-thumb-film-walk, 1-view-to-edit) shows a new position at least every 20ms once it starts moving, as Edit to View already does
On the long captioned sample, the main thread is busy for well under half of the 0.8s after Cmd-2 (it is about 650 to 750ms today)
View mode playback is no slower
